name: Ischgl
kurzbeschreibung: Ischgl in Paznaun valley: world-famous Silvretta Arena with 239 km of slopes, legendary Top of the Mountain Concerts, and modern Silvretta Therme.
beschreibung:
Overview

The municipality of Ischgl lies at an altitude of 1,377 metres above sea level in the rear Paznaun valley between the Silvretta and Verwall mountain groups in the Tyrolean Oberland. What once began as a modest mountain farming village has evolved into one of the world's most renowned winter sports and lifestyle metropolises in the Alps. With the cross-border Silvretta Arena seamlessly linking Ischgl to the Swiss duty-free exclave of Samnaun, spectacular open-air summit concerts, and cutting-edge infrastructure, the resort captivates hundreds of thousands of active holidaymakers from around the globe every year.

Silvretta Arena, Concerts & Wellness

The beating heart of tourism is the Silvretta Arena Ischgl-Samnaun: boasting 239 kilometres of slopes, 46 state-of-the-art cable cars and ski lifts, and descents up to 2,872 metres above sea level (Greitspitze), the ski area ranks among the largest and most snow-reliable regions in Austria. The annual Top of the Mountain Concerts enjoy legendary worldwide cult status: on the monumental open-air stage on the Idalp (2,320 m), global megastars like Elton John, Robbie Williams, Alicia Keys, and Helene Fischer perform in front of tens of thousands of fans against a majestic high-alpine winter backdrop to mark the season opening in late November, Easter, and the grand season finale. In summer, the valley transforms into a premier hiking and mountain biking paradise with a route network exceeding 1,000 kilometres. Among the most thrilling adventures is the Ischgl Skyfly – a two-kilometre zip line where thrill-seekers glide over the Kitzloch gorge towards the valley at speeds of up to 85 km/h. An architectural masterpiece is the Silvretta Therme, opened in December 2022: a pioneering wellness and spa resort featuring over 1,000 m² of water surface, panoramic pools, and an expansive sauna world.

Visit & Getting There

The winter season of the Silvretta Arena reliably spans from late November to early May; in summer, the cable cars operate daily from late June to mid-October from 08:30 to 16:30. Silvretta ski pass (as of 2025/2026): adult day ticket from approx. €76.00, youth/seniors approx. €68.00, children approx. €45.00 (concert access is included in the valid ski pass). Silvretta Therme: 3-hour ticket from approx. €36.00, day ticket approx. €49.00. With the Silvretta Card Premium in summer, cable cars and local public transport are included without limit. Travel by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 or Arlbergschnellstraße S16 to the Pians exit, from there along the B188 (Paznauntalstraße) for approx. 25 km directly to Ischgl; parking garages (e.g. Florianigarage) are available at the entrance to town. By public transport: ÖBB/Railjet to Landeck-Zams station, from where VVT bus line 260 runs every half hour directly to the centre of Ischgl (travel time approx. 50 minutes).

Tips

Thanks to modern valley stations, escalators, pedestrian tunnels, and barrier-free large-capacity gondolas, the cable cars and mountain restaurants on the Idalp are exceptionally accessible for guests with mobility impairments and strollers. Visitors travelling in summer should hike the cross-border Schmugglerrunde or explore the duty-free shopping promenade in neighbouring Samnaun.

oeffnungszeiten: Skibetrieb Ende Nov bis Anfang Mai tgl. 08:30–16:00 Uhr; Sommer Jun–Okt; Therme tgl. 10:00–22:00 Uhr
